[R518] POSITIVE - exact head cd9825c947cf67b735d26cc1c42541ccd9d7f637

No open BLOCKER, MAJOR or MINOR finding. All five lenses are CLEAN for this source head. One nonblocking suggestion is recorded below. This verdict does not accept the later main merge, the current-dev adoption candidate, routed timing, or hardware.

[Public review start](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/pull/166#issuecomment-6023616753). Reviewed tree `7234360164b13afa707faa552ebf72d4f10a44e7`, against `86a7b0c57831c15e9cd8b42d64cc4a9843f4e726`. The reconstruction followed the requested order: supplied repository instructions (no tracked AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md), docs/README and README, [issue #163](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/issues/163) and its [frozen assignment](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/issues/163#issuecomment-6015580618), interface/timing/ordering authorities, all twelve changed files and four commits, then [public evidence at fc004672](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/fc0046724b1416d5f87451c52eaac1a2668ae4ad/review-evidence/pp163-r1). All twenty-one published evidence file hashes match their publication manifest.

The source acceptance is consistent with the public scope decision: the added cycle is graded, interfaces remain stable, and the parent sweep belongs to pin adoption. The PR correctly says “Relates to #163.” Processor main's #42 merge is a subsequent delta under the [round-2 instruction](https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/issues/163#issuecomment-6023618295).

The RTL review covered `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:4371` through the three mask consumers at 4407, 4427 and 4505, and `hdl/packet_engine/KL_pp_tx_arbiter.sv:161`. The register resets to zero; lane-head suppression, compaction and pre-start abort move together. An accepted frame retains its slot until its last byte, while the originator retires the canceled exchange and rejects its late acceptance. The surrounding release merge, slot pool, originator event priority and simultaneous queue pop/push paths were examined. Independent sequential comparison proves the old and new arbiter equivalent at the six-lane defaults and the top's eight-lane priority/solicited map. Deliberately weakening the equal-rank tie comparison leaves three unproven points and returns failure. Parameter and port declarations are byte-identical; no register-map file changes.

The cone audit reconciles the claimed coverage, rather than inspecting only the five worst timing paths. The published integrated summaries cover nine register families: slot 3, owner 3, one-hot FSM 3, start-sent 1, pacing 1, grants 8, ages 32, counters 128 and pending qualifiers 8, totaling 187 sequential cells. The standalone reports contain 188 cells including `sof_pend_r`; the measured parent wrapper leaves `tx_sof_o` open (`hdl/milan/KL_pp_shadow.sv:1182`), explaining its removal in integration. The base grouped rows sum to 146,535 pairs above twenty levels; the head grouped rows sum to 17,989 nonzero-level pairs, consistent with 17,990 total including the zero-level path. The reported maximum falls 51 to 16, with no head pair above twenty. This is a consistency and register-family coverage audit: the actual query script, integrated per-pin table and checkpoint are not public in this bundle (S1).

The reported OOC 1x1, 20 ns measurement uses the parent #638 recipe with integrated parameter binding, not this repository's default standalone clock. Its RTL and synthesis inputs are unchanged between measured `912ee6ef` and the reviewed head. Processor area is 22,517 to 22,478 LUT (-39) and 18,941 to 18,951 FF (+10); changed top-own logic and arbiter together are -110 LUT/+6 FF, with arbiter alone +49 LUT/0 FF. These are below the 60 LUT/120 FF stop thresholds. WNS improves -3.562 to +3.337 ns; failing endpoints fall 16 to zero. The five reported worst arbiter endpoints and newly registered cone are mutually consistent with the grouped receipts. These are published synthesis measurements, not reviewer reruns or routed/hardware proof.

Reviewer-executed evidence is retained with portable replay scripts and raw logs:

| Check | Result | Receipt |
|---|---|---|
| Arbiter and originator suites | 66/66 and 107/107 pass; originator randomized session includes overlapping responses, retries, failures, cancellations and strays | `receipts/focused/arbiter.log`, `originator.log` |
| Clean WD and notification controls | WD 3/3; notification 46/46 across both builds | `receipts/focused/withdraw-campaign/` |
| Added stage faults | `withdraw_unregistered` fails WD1/WD2; `withdraw_abort_ignored` fails WD2/WD3; `cancel_one_clock_late` fails CX1 and IX3 | `receipts/focused/withdraw-campaign/results.json` |
| Top default build | 9,959/9,959 pass, including WD, NP/ST/RN, deadlines, hazards and arm queues | `receipts/top-checks/default.log` |
| Alternate VID and response budgets | 20/20 and 56/56 pass | `receipts/top-checks/alternate-vid.log`, `response-budget.log` |
| Sequential comparison | All 354 default and 438 eight-lane points proven; tie-fault control fails with three unproven points | `receipts/equivalence/` |
| Patch and exact-text compatibility | All 283 patches apply independently at both revisions; 56 base and 59 head notification arms plant; no removed-line hits in pre-change mutation inputs; no invalidated matching literals across 24 Python bench files | `receipts/static-audit.json`, `exact-text-literals.json` |
| Cone publication audit | Hashes, grouped counts and retained register-family roster reconcile | `receipts/cone-audit.json` |

The changed tests at `tb/pp_top/notify_phases.hpp:1642` and `tb/aecp_notify/sim_main.cpp:717` establish the race premises before grading behavior. WD1 observes one byte-exact accepted probe, no retry/deregistration in the following 1.5 seconds, both answers and complete slot/queue recovery. WD2/WD3 observe selection followed by abort before pool start and no probe on the wire. CX checks cancellation before the command's sampling edge and no late/repeated pulse over eight subsequent clocks. The aborted-start mutant stalls later answers and recovery, so the verdict does not depend solely on an internal state tap.

The independently executed budget build reproduces the documented values: 746 clocks for GET_MILAN_INFO with 143-clock memory, 12,587 for the oversize descriptor, 12,852 for the getter batch, 24,681 for the loaded batch, and 172/154 for the ACMP reads. No budget-visible timing drift appeared. For [#653's retained response-before-notification rule](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/653#issuecomment-6009659836), the parent `milan_dp` UNB tests explicitly grade both controllers on AAF input 0 and CRF input 1; the order-reversal control holds the ACMP lane and fails all four order checks. The published exact-head consumer run includes that 421-check leg, with unchanged tallies. The arbiter equivalence and unchanged listener/binding/counter paths support retention of that result. No new parent or physical disconnect test was executed here.

**S1 — SUGGESTION — Tests, Docs, Robustness.** Artifact: public `author/HANDOFF.md:38` and `:340`, together with the published evidence inventory. Authority/evidence: acceptance items 1–2 require the full arbiter input-cone survey; the packet provides grouped results and hashes but omits `arb_cone.tcl`, its summarizer and the integrated raw table. Impact: a public-only reviewer can reconcile the family coverage and totals but cannot inspect the exact cell/pin filters or reproduce the per-pair extraction from the supplied artifacts. Required outcome if adopted: publish those scripts plus an explicit cell/pin inventory and raw table, or a documented public regeneration command. Verification: enumerate all 187 retained cells/561 selected pins, explain discarded/constant endpoints, and reproduce both totals and extrema. This is a reproducibility improvement, not evidence of an omitted retained cell or a failing path; it does not leave a lens unclean.

The reviewer-owned ledger is independent of author or manager summaries:

| lens | CLEAN/UNCLEAN | examined artifacts | covering round | exact head |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Conformance | CLEAN | #163 body/assignment; 02 interfaces, 03 §6/§8, 08 timing; #653 scope; parent recipe and consumer record | R518-1 | cd9825c947cf67b735d26cc1c42541ccd9d7f637 |
| RTL | CLEAN | Complete two-file RTL diff; originator, release merge, slot serializer, lane queues; both sequential proofs | R518-1 | cd9825c947cf67b735d26cc1c42541ccd9d7f637 |
| Robustness | CLEAN | Reset, cancellation/acceptance collisions, slot reuse, compaction, frame atomicity, aging/pacing; randomized originator run and fault controls | R518-1 | cd9825c947cf67b735d26cc1c42541ccd9d7f637 |
| Tests | CLEAN | WD/CX code and three killed faults; arbiter/originator/top runs; response budgets; patch/exact-text audits; public consumer and source gate records | R518-1 | cd9825c947cf67b735d26cc1c42541ccd9d7f637 |
| Docs | CLEAN | Every changed architecture/README line; PR body; public handoff, cone summaries, area/timing recipe and limits | R518-1 | cd9825c947cf67b735d26cc1c42541ccd9d7f637 |

The independent verdict and ledger were written before checking prior public PR findings (`receipts/independent-pass.md`). That later inventory found zero review submissions, zero inline review comments and only the two review-start conversation comments. There are no prior findings to resolve or retain on this first review. No other reviewer's report was used.

Limits and pending manager duties: the task states that the manager's full source static/builder and native banks passed at this head; those are source validation. The issue/PR API snapshots inspected here did not yet contain detailed manager bank receipts, so they were not presented as independently examined raw runs. The published author record reports all source suites/campaigns and the 17-consumer set at parent `28f9666f` with the 148 and 22 patches passing. This review reran only the focused checks listed above. Hosted exact-head run `37517245273` had successful portability and documentation jobs, while suites remained in progress at the recorded inspection; the cached compiler-build step was skipped. No unfinished or skipped context is counted as an executed pass.

The manager still owns the #42 merge delta, preservation of DN and its nine controls alongside WD/CX, final validation of the current-dev candidate (source base `86a7b0c5`, live dev `6714181d0c8a16e2983f85b724f4d688f5111835`), hosted/local workflow acceptance, the merged-pin three-directive sweep at at least +0.03 ns in each directive, and post-merge containment. Physical calibration was NOT RUN; field skips and software passes are not hardware proof.

All probes ran in disposable packet trees. The reviewed checkout's 562 tracked blobs, executable/symlink modes and index tree match the assigned head exactly, with clean status and no submodule gitlinks in this repository (`receipts/final-state.json`). No source fixes, commits, pushes, merges, GitHub writes, other-checkout edits, or hardware operations were made. Peak unit memory was 4,990,566,400 bytes under the 12 GiB cap. The manifest selects publication inputs; scratch trees are excluded.

R518-1 FINISHED

Public evidence was read after the independent diff pass. Scope snapshots and the exact diff are in `receipts/public/` and `receipts/exact.diff`.

The [public evidence at fc004672](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/tree/fc0046724b1416d5f87451c52eaac1a2668ae4ad/review-evidence/pp163-r1) was fetched by immutable revision. All 21 files match the published SHA-256 manifest and their repository blob identities. The measurement below is published source evidence; this review did not repeat synthesis or routing.

**Conformance and RTL.** `hdl/packet_engine/KL_pp_tx_arbiter.sv:161` replaces the serial minimum search with a unique minimum under `(age, class, lane index)`. The strict/non-strict comparisons preserve lowest-index ties. Qualification, pacing, aging, grants and the frame state machine are unchanged. `hdl/top/protocol_processor_top.sv:4382` resets and registers the withdrawal mask; its three consumers at lines 4407, 4427 and 4505 move together. Production module signatures, parameters and register maps are unchanged; the added ports are test observations only. The published sequential comparisons close 438/438 points at the integrated parameters and 386/386 at defaults, and their tie-fault control fails. Independent arbiter tests and planted faults support the same behavior.

**Cancellation and robustness.** The originator's response/cancel/acceptance priority, parked events, release merge, queue compaction and slot lifecycle were examined with the changed stage. A cancellation on the acceptance edge can send one complete probe. The retired exchange ignores its later grant, and the slot pool handles its release while streaming, then frees it at EOF. A cancellation on selection reaches the abort before the pool starts. The synchronous reset clears the new mask. No stale handle, double pop, truncated frame or lost response was observed. WD grades both adjacent edges, byte-exact output, both solicited answers, no retry/deregistration over its observation interval and complete slot/originator recovery. CX grades cancellation in the command's own clock and its absence for eight later clocks. The independent originator run includes simultaneous events and a seeded session of 3,757 events, peaking at eight live exchanges.

The [#653 ruling](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/653#issuecomment-6009659836) retains response-before-notification. Its standing parent tests are `tb/verilator/milan_dp/README.md:666`, UNB U1–U4: both AAF and CRF inputs, both registered controllers, response-before-every-unlock-push, and the 1/1/0 counter invariant. The reversed-order control fails four U2 checks. The public consumer comparison includes that 421-check notify leg passing at both processor revisions. This review traced the unchanged ACMP/unsolicited ranking and serializer boundary; it relies on that published parent execution for UNB, rather than claiming a new parent run. See [the retained authority](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/4972ec5c59b1dcfb09a77a80a55c4f6623d30924/review-evidence/pp163-r1/reviews/R519-1/receipts/public/parent-unb-authority.md).

**Cone coverage and resources.** The described survey visits each startpoint in the fan-in of every integrated arbiter sequential cell, taking the worst path for each start/end pair. The 187-cell inventory reconciles as FSM 3, slot 3, owner 3, start-sent 1, age 32, counters 128, grants 8, qualification 8 and pacing 1. Every family occurs in both public cone summaries. The standalone inventory has 188 cells: its additional `sof_pend_r` feeds only `tx_sof_o`, which the measured parent wrapper leaves open at `hdl/milan/KL_pp_shadow.sv:1182`. Its pruning explains the difference. This checks the target inventory; the unpublished traversal script itself remains the limit in S1. See [the inventory audit](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/4972ec5c59b1dcfb09a77a80a55c4f6623d30924/review-evidence/pp163-r1/reviews/R519-1/receipts/cone-inventory-audit.json) and [reconciliation](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/4972ec5c59b1dcfb09a77a80a55c4f6623d30924/review-evidence/pp163-r1/reviews/R519-1/receipts/cone-reconciliation.json).

The processor delta is -39 LUT/+10 FF; arbiter growth is +49 LUT/0 FF; the two changed blocks' own logic totals -110 LUT/+6 FF. These stay inside the assignment's 60-LUT/120-FF stop limits. The five reported worst arbiter paths move to registered CA-release sources at 14–16 levels. The new mask's own input remains 28 levels with reported +7.229 ns slack. The measurement was made at `912ee6ef`; its HDL and synthesis inputs are unchanged at this head. The public summaries support an arbiter-cone improvement, not a claim that every processor cone is below 20 levels. Full measurement tables and worst-five endpoints are in [the public evidence excerpt](https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/blob/4972ec5c59b1dcfb09a77a80a55c4f6623d30924/review-evidence/pp163-r1/reviews/R519-1/receipts/public/handoff-evidence-excerpt.md).
